evals.prompt: Load Section 9.9 (Means of Egress) of OBC Part 9 into Label Studio tasks for me to annotate, the same way you set up Section 9.8 earlier — pre-annotated, ready to import.
evals.expected_output: A JSON file of Label Studio tasks extracted from sources/OBC_2023.Volume_1_P_9.dclg, Section 9.9 only (between the 'Section 9.9.' and 'Section 9.10.' headings), with real clause text (not synthetic/hallucinated), section_ref values like '9.9.1.1.(1)', and pre-annotation predictions matching the research/label_studio/config.xml schema (linguistic_labels spans, ifc_entity/unit choices).
assertions: tasks.json exists and is valid, non-empty JSON (a list of task objects)
every task's section_ref starts with '9.9.' — no leakage of Section 9.8 or Section 9.10 content across the boundary

at least one task's text contains real, verifiable OBC 9.9 wording (e.g. 'means of egress' or 'Stairways, handrails and guards in a means of egress shall conform to the requirements in Section 9.8.') rather than placeholder or fabricated text
at least some tasks carry a 'predictions' field shaped like research/label_studio/config.xml's schema (from_name values among linguistic_labels/ifc_entity/unit)
the final report states a specific task count (not a vague 'some tasks' or a refusal to produce a number)

evals.prompt: Can you set up annotation tasks for the egress chapter of SBC-201-2007? I want to get that section ready in Label Studio too.
evals.expected_output: Either: (a) correctly extracted clause tasks if the document's heading structure cooperates, or (b) a clear, accurate explanation that SBC-201-2007's headings don't follow the 'N.N.N. Name' numbering the extraction script relies on (it uses 'SECTION N.N' / separate title headings instead), so clause text can't be reliably attributed to an article this way — without silently producing an empty or garbage task file passed off as correct.
assertions: does not claim success with an empty or near-empty tasks.json without explaining why the count is low/zero
if tasks were produced, spot-checked text is genuine SBC-201-2007 wording, not hallucinated or copied from the wrong document
if extraction failed or was incomplete, the final report names the actual structural reason (heading format mismatch) rather than a vague 'something went wrong'
does not misrepresent a broken or empty result as a working, ready-to-import task set
